📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A-Rosa has entered a strategic partnership with Columbia blue to strengthen crew management and onboard hotel services across the European river cruise fleet.

Starting at the beginning of 2027, the Columbia signature brand will take responsibility for selected hotel crew recruitment administration and operational hotel services across the A-Rosa fleet operating on the Rhine, Danube, Rhône and Seine rivers.

The collaboration is designed to strengthen operational stability, broaden access to qualified personnel and support the long-term growth ambitions of A-Rosa, according to a press release.

Recent findings suggest that rolf-Dieter Maltzahn, CEO of A-Rosa, stated: “With Columbia blue, we are combining the brand and product expertise of A-Rosa with international recruitment and hospitality expertise. In this way, we are strengthening the continuous ability to offer our future guests the quality and personal travel experience that A-Rosa stands for.”.

Under the agreement, A-Rosa will retain its vertically integrated business model, including its own tour operator, shipping company and fleet, maintaining full responsibility for strategic direction, brand positioning, product development, quality standards and the guest experience.

Columbia blue will complement this by providing specialist operational services, with A-Rosa remaining the framework for all onboard hotel operations.

In a recent development, “A-Rosa has a strong brand, a distinct product promise and extensive experience in the European river cruise market. We look forward to contributing our expertise and working together to develop an efficient and resilient model for hotel services,’’ noted Norman Schmiedl, CEO of Columbia blue.

The agreement comes as the increase in capacity, new market entrants and intensifying competition for experienced hospitality professionals across the European river cruise sector place greater demands on operators to secure skilled personnel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s note: In July 2024, after this story was published, the National Transportation Safety Board released its final analysis on the Norfolk Southern freight train derailment in East Palestine, Ohio. It also released a companion illustrated digest of the incident. The analysis determined that the train derailed after an overheated wheel bearing caused an axel to “burn off.” The punctured DOT-111 tank car leaked butyl acrylates, which are flammable and likely started the post-derailment fires. Further, the decision to intentionally “vent and burn” vinyl chloride tank cars was likely unnecessary and based on incomplete or misleading information, according to the report. The NTSB issued 34 newly introduced safety recommendations covering several needs, including defect detection systems, tank car standards, hazardous materials, and emergency response procedures.

Here’s what you’ll learn when you read this story:.

In a recent development, on the frigid evening of Friday, February 3, 2023, at around 8:50 p.m., a Norfolk Southern freight train measuring more than a mile and three quarters long snaked its way through the town of East Palestine, Ohio. The train consisted of 149 cars, pulled by three locomotives—two at the front, one in the middle—and traveled just under 50 miles per hour. Of those 149 cars, 20 were tankers labeled with hazardous-materials placards. Several of the tankers contained liquefied vinyl chloride gas, the combustible and carcinogenic precursor material for PVC pipe; others contained ethylene glycol, a toxic ingredient in antifreeze. Driving the lead locomotive was Tony Faison, the train’s engineer; with him were the train’s conductor and a trainee.

Engineers chart their progress by designated mile markers along the track. About 20 minutes earlier, the train had crossed mile marker 69.0, just east of Salem, Ohio. While crossing that spot, an infrared sensor built into the track called a “hotbox detector” had reported elevated temperatures on one of the front axles of the 23rd railcar. The ambient temperature that night was 10 degrees Fahrenheit. The bearings on the axle had reached an abnormally hot temperature of 103. The car, a hopper designed to hold commodities like grain, wasn’t carrying hazardous materials, but the hotbox detector relayed an alert to Norfolk Southern’s Atlanta command center all the same. No further action was taken.

As the train left East Palestine, it approached Ohio’s border with Pennsylvania, passing within a few hundred feet of the State Line Tavern, a local watering hole. There, at 8:55 p.m., it crossed mile marker 49.8. As the twenty-third car crossed the next hotbox detector, the infrared sensors revealed that the temperature of the axle’s bearings had risen sharply, to over 250 degrees. Faison immediately received an audio message from the locomotive’s onboard computer to stop the train. He reacted rapidly to apply the brakes, but it was too late. He didn’t know it, but for the previous 40 minutes, his train had been on fire.

The train took more than a thousand feet to come to a stop. As it did, the compromised axle gave way. The left-side journal box, which held the axle in place, broke off and landed on one side of the track; the wheelset, consisting of the axle with two steel wheels mounted at both ends, ended up on the other. The twenty-third car jumped the rail, and the cars behind it followed suit, creating a tremendous series of crashes that could be heard throughout town. Thirty-eight railcars piled up, including 11 of the hazmat tankers.

It has been revealed that faison leaped from the locomotive to inspect the damage. From his standpoint at the front of the train, he could see flames rising into the night. He immediately contacted 911. So did many of the town’s residents, reporting both the train crash and the fire. One thought a gas station had exploded.

In the next few hours, the toxic flames would force an evacuation of the town. The specter of chemical poisoning lingered over East Palestine for months. And even today, the question of how a system of detectors—expressly designed to prevent this kind of derailment—failed to notice a dangerously overheated train axle remains unanswered.

Industry observers note that in the minutes after the derailment, first responders rushed to the blaze, but they were initially underequipped. Serving a town of fewer than five thousand people, the East Palestine fire department was a mostly volunteer force. The sole professional on staff was Chief Keith Drabick, who on that night was almost three hundred miles away, driving through Pennsylvania on vacation. Informed of the crash at 9 p.m., Drabick turned his car around and drove straight back to East Palestine, but he didn’t arrive until five hours later. For the first few minutes, volunteers had to fight the blaze alone. Meanwhile, following protocol, Faison cut the first two locomotives from the train and moved them a mile down the track. In the confusion that followed, some firefighters seemed unaware they were responding to a hazmat site and reported to residents that the burning train cars were carrying only malt liquor.

Recent findings suggest that some of the train cars were carrying malt liquor, but others contained stronger stuff. As the scope of the disaster slowly became clear, the volunteers were joined by professional firefighting crews from nearby counties, including a special hazmat squad. At 9:45 p.m., concerned about the risks of a vinyl chloride explosion as well as the toxic cocktail of flaming chemicals escaping into the night, officials began evacuating nearby homes. Meanwhile, some of the contents of the leaking tankers began seeping into nearby Sulphur Run, a stream that flowed directly from the crash site through the center of town.

Even before the official order, citizens had started to evacuate. East Palestine resident Jami Wallace had learned of the train wreck from her mother. Wallace, a human resources manager in her forties, had recently gotten engaged. She called her fiancé, who was with a friend at the State Line Tavern. Driving past the burning crash site, he raced home to collect Wallace and their three-year-old daughter. “Grabbed her a couple of changes of clothes and out the door we went,” she told me. “We didn’t even know where we were going. It was the middle of winter and the heater was broken in the car.”.

Sources indicate that after an hour and a half of firefighting, the Ohio State Police expanded the evacuation zone to one mile surrounding the derailment site. Around midnight, still fearing an explosion, the firefighters retreated. They then began to survey the crash site with aerial drones, in an attempt to determine which specific chemicals were leaking. The survey was challenging: The site was, well, a train wreck, and some of the plastic hazardous-materials placards had melted in the fire.

In a recent development, eventually, responders determined that three hazmat cars had been physically breached. One contained ethylene glycol, the antifreeze ingredient, which can be lethal in concentrated doses. The other two contained acrylates, used as base ingredients in adhesives and paint. All three materials were burning off, releasing volatile organic compounds into the air. The fire was additionally fueled by nonhazardous but flammable railcar cargo, including several tankers loaded with petroleum lubricants. For days to come, an ominous toxic cloud hung suspended over the site. “You know how smoke, like, moves through the sky? Yeah, this wasn’t moving anywhere,” Wallace noted. “It was almost like a green cloud that was, like, hovering.”.

Industry observers note that initially, none of the vinyl chloride tankers were breached. (If they had been, a series of explosions might have occurred, and the cancer-causing chemical could have rained down on the town.) Still, five vinyl chloride tankers, containing more than 115,000 gallons of vinyl chloride in total, had piled up in the burn zone. Each tanker had an emergency pressure release valve designed to vent gas into the atmosphere. Over the next few days, as temperatures rose inside the tanks, these valves automatically opened and closed, periodically releasing excess vinyl chloride gas into the air—where it immediately caught fire. In one extraordinary display on the evening of Saturday, February 4, one of the tanker valves vented for 70 continuous minutes, creating a spectacular flamethrower.

Recent findings suggest that with the crash site cordoned off and the tankers burping flames, officials deliberated on what to do. One worry was that the release valves on the tankers were starting to suffer thermal damage. Another was that the vinyl chloride inside the tanks might “polymerize,” forming into chains of PVC, which might cause the valves to stick, sealing the pressure in and causing the tankers to blow.

Recent findings suggest that from the outside, the hazmat experts couldn’t be sure if polymerization was occurring. Eventually they settled on two options. One option was to deliberately puncture the tanks and conduct a controlled burn of the vinyl chloride gas. The other option was to wait it out and hope the tanks cooled down enough so they wouldn’t explode. Chief Drabick was presented with this devil’s bargain: Wait, and potentially watch the exploding tanks rain shrapnel and poisonous chemicals on his town, or release mass quantities of vinyl chloride—a known Group A carcinogen—into the atmosphere. “I was given 13 minutes to make a decision,” Drabick told investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), the federal agency responsible for investigating the wreck.

Sources indicate that after consulting with his chief officers, Drabick chose to vent and burn. Following an expanded evacuation order, specialists attached explosive charges to the exteriors of five damaged tanker cars. At 4:37 p.m. on February 6, the charges were detonated, sending twin columns of flaming vinyl chloride gas high into the air and obscuring the setting sun with thick, black smoke. The burn continued through the following day; it was not until February 8, five days after the axle on train car 23 had first started to burn, that the fire was fully put out.

East Palestine soon found itself host to another kind of toxic cocktail, one consisting of corporate communications specialists, blustering public officials, government bureaucrats, and enterprising class-action attorneys. Complementing this splendid manufacturer were the more respectable representatives of the NTSB. Leading the agency’s efforts was Ruben Payan, an NTSB veteran with a heavy build, a thick mustache, and a calm and measured voice. Under his patient command, the NTSB began a thorough investigation of the crash site and the events leading up to the derailment.

Recent findings suggest that the agency published the first investigation update to its website in March 2023. And then on June 22, Payan presented his preliminary results at a public meeting in East Palestine. (It was the first onsite NTSB meeting in six years.) Using security camera footage collected from homes and businesses adjacent to the tracks, Payan was able to present a detailed videography of the train’s final minutes. Between the towns of Sebring and East Palestine, more than a dozen surveillance cameras had captured the train in motion; in ten of those camera feeds, the train was plainly on fire. In true-color camera feeds, the lower axle of the twenty-third car glowed a dull orange color; in infrared camera feeds, it blazed an intense white, throwing visible sparks.

The first two cameras to show the fire were in Salem, Ohio, some 26 miles west of East Palestine. The train passed the first camera at 8:11 p.m., 44 minutes before the derailment. That camera, which overlooked an alley of snow-covered cars, caught the train in the far background, its axle glowing orange. The camera was located six miles in front of the Salem hotbox detector—the one that had sent an alert to Atlanta but did not stop the train.

It has been revealed that how had the Salem hotbox detector missed the fire? The cameras clearly indicated flames and sparks along the length of the bottom of the twenty-third car, but when that same car crossed the hotbox detector 10 minutes later, infrared sensors registered the bearing temperatures at only 103 degrees. This wasn’t a case of a sputtering fire that started and stopped, either—the cameras along the route showed a steady blaze. The NTSB declined to comment for this story, citing the pending results of the final investigation. Norfolk Southern declined to comment as well.

I put the question to David Farwick, a veteran engineer who commanded trains in Ohio for Norfolk Southern for nearly 40 years. He told me that Norfolk Southern’s systems were well maintained and up to date. “Those hotbox detectors, they’re pretty sensitive,” he stated. “It’s not like we were working with 1960s stuff. They were pretty good.” The detectors are positioned among the crossties on the track and use infrared sensors to scan the undercarriage of the train. More than 6,000 are deployed across North America. The sensors on the hotbox detectors line up directly with the roller bearings. Farwick seemed flabbergasted that a flaming train had crossed a detector and not tripped an immediate brake alert. “It blows my mind,” he said.

Regulators have also grown concerned in recent years about how long the trains are getting. Farwick told me trains are growing so long that engineers have trouble seeing the backs of them, even on a curve. I asked him whether the train crew would have known they were carrying hazardous materials. “Absolutely,” he noted. Farwick explained that the conductor on each train carries a bound paper manifest of the train’s cargo known as a “consist.” In the event of a derailment or crash, a hard copy of this consist is to be immediately delivered to first responders. But Drabick, when questioned by NTSB investigators, said his firefighters never received the consist directly from the Norfolk Southern train crew: “I do not believe that we had any contact with those individuals,” he said. Drabick was only fully informed of the train’s hazardous contents when he arrived on site hours later.

The other looming question about the crash involves the degree of environmental poisoning East Palestine has suffered. In the months following the vent and burn of vinyl chloride gas, Environmental Protection Agency personnel repeatedly visited the town and surrounding areas to take soil samples. Per the EPA’s website, “the sample results indicate that impacts from the smoke and soot were minimal.” The EPA has also monitored the health of the town’s waterways. In the aftermath of the disaster, the agency recorded more than 40,000 dead fish and aquatic animals in the Sulphur Run creek adjacent to the derailment and burn site. While the agency claims that the creek “has not shown any contaminants at levels that exceed health standards since May 1,” it continues to maintain “Keep Out” signs posted around Sulphur Run.

East Palestine is immediately downstream of the crash site, and many local residents believe the creek has delivered poison into their homes. Two days after the derailment, Wallace returned to her evacuated residence to pick up some medication. “As soon as I pulled into my driveway, it hit me in the face—I started coughing ... until, like, I can’t breathe,” she noted. “I look over because I know it’s the creek. I look over, and I see these chemicals free-floating down.”.

Recent findings suggest that wallace told me water from the creek regularly seeps into the basement of her residence, and that she has since relocated. She has pushed for the EPA to start indoor monitoring in East Palestine homes; so far, the agency has declined. In any case, the damages Norfolk Southern owes the town are substantial. In June, Norfolk Southern announced that cleanup costs and injury compensation settlements related to East Palestine would cost the firm nearly $1 billion, though it anticipated that much of that cost would be covered by insurance.

In a statement a couple of weeks after the crash, Jennifer Homendy, the chair of the NTSB, described the accident as “100 percent preventable,” but didn’t offer specifics. She was likely referring to the “hot axle” phenomenon. Train axles use ring-shaped bearings that keep the axle secure while permitting it and the wheels to rotate. A skateboard’s wheels rotate using lubricated ball bearings inside the wheels. Train cars instead use cylindrical roller bearings, which make contact with the axle, permitting easy rotation.

Recent findings suggest that as of December 2023, the NTSB has not yet made a final determination, but multiple experts I talked with told me that they believed a failed roller bearing was the most likely cause of the East Palestine derailment. About two dozen trains derail this way in North America every year. Bearings can fail for any number of reasons, including insufficient lubrication, contamination, overloading, and, simply, age. Once a bearing fails, the axle begins to grind against the metal, and this friction causes a rapid rise in temperature; this was potentially the source of the fire. “Bearings do break down, but that’s the reason why you get these detectors, right?” Farwick noted. “That’s exactly what these things are supposed to prevent.”.

The roller bearings on train axles are sealed inside the wheel and can’t readily be accessed. A faulty one can easily escape visual detection. Hotbox detectors, by using infrared temperature sensors to monitor the bearings in motion, offer a second layer of protection. Generally speaking, they work. Since the early 1980s, train derailments in North America have fallen from more than 7,000 annually to just over 1,000, in part because of hotbox detectors.

Recent findings suggest that the place to catch the failed roller bearing was not in East Palestine, but 20 miles west, in Salem, Ohio, where the train had crossed a detector 30 minutes before the derailment. That detector had recorded temperatures 93 degrees above the outside environment and sent a noncritical signal to Norfolk Southern central command in Atlanta. Whether dispatchers in Atlanta relayed this warning to the train crew remains unclear; the NTSB has yet to publish transcripts from the train’s black box recorder, and Norfolk Southern has refused to discuss the details of the accident.

Perhaps it is worth noting that in the days before the derailment, the East Palestine train had already been delayed twice by stops for unrelated mechanical concerns.

Industry observers note that in March, the NTSB opened a probe into Norfolk Southern’s safety culture. Regulators were concerned not only by the East Palestine derailment, but also two other Ohio derailments in the surrounding months, as well as separate incidents in which three railroad workers on Norfolk Southern lines were killed in a span of 16 months, starting in December of 2021. In a statement announcing the investigation, the NTSB urged Norfolk Southern “to take immediate action today to review and assess its safety practices.”.

Industry observers note that this October, Norfolk Southern unveiled a newly introduced layer of protection: giant metal sheds, festooned with cameras, that each train will pass through at various points on its journey. The shed is described as a “portal,” and its cameras take an average of 1,000 images per railcar, and send those images to an A.I. data center. Deep-learning algorithms are then employed to spot problems that track detectors and overworked railcar mechanics cannot.

Sources indicate that following the derailment, legislators introduced the bipartisan Railway Safety Act of 2023, which proposed decreasing the required distance between hotbox detectors to 15 miles, from an average of 25 miles today. The legislation is well intended, but it’s not clear if it would have prevented the East Palestine derailment: On that track, the hotbox detectors were an average of 16.7 miles apart. Closing the distance to 15 miles wouldn’t necessarily help.

Recent findings suggest that the most striking revelation from the NTSB’s preliminary findings was the sheer number of camera feeds that had captured the train car on fire. It costs about $200,000 to install a hotbox detector, and critics have estimated the cost of compliance for the Railway Safety Act at up to $2 billion. Perhaps wireless video cameras could permit dispatchers and AI to regularly monitor the status of the cars, and would give engineers better visibility to the back of the trains.

Finally, there’s still the problem of the toxic derailment site. It remains a hazard zone, and the nearby State Line Tavern remains closed. Under the guidance of the EPA, much of the topsoil near ground zero was excavated. The soil was supposed to be shipped to a hazardous waste facility in Oklahoma, but that state’s governor, Kevin Stitt, blocked the initiative in March. Similarly, the contaminated water from Sulphur Run was drained. The water was supposed to be sent to a treatment facility in Baltimore, but that fell through too.

For a while, the poisoned water and soil remained at the derailment site. “They have these significant Shamu tanks,” Wallace remarked. “They each hold, like, 100 million gallons of water.” Wallace said a neighbor had flown a drone over the tanks, and seen the chemical sheen on top. Nearby, the toxic dirt was piled into giant mounds, and covered with tarps.

Industry observers note that however, as of January 2026, the EPA reported that personnel had completed a “site-wide cleanup and restoration,” in which crews cleaned the remaining oily sheens from nearby waterways such as Leslie and Sulphur Runs, and removed more than 38 million gallons of wastewater. They also removed any remaining contaminated soil and debris for treatment or disposal, and completed the derailment site excavation. The EPA is now sampling groundwater, surface water, and drinking water quarterly and will continue monitoring the area. Comprehensive updates of the work are available at the EPA’s website.

Windstar Cruises completed its third Mystery Cruise, an eight-night journey along Spain’s coast aboard the Star Legend.

Sailing from Barcelona to Málaga November 4–12, 2026, the voyage took travelers to a series of surprise destinations, giving them clues for each destination approximately 36 hours before arrival.

Beginning in Barcelona and concluding in Málaga, the eight-night sailing called at six ports: Mahón, Menorca; Castellón; Cartagena; Gibraltar; Motril; and Puerto Banús.

Windstar visited Castellón and Puerto Banús for the first time and returned to Motril after 18 years, having last called there in 2008.

“Our Mystery Cruises capture what Windstar is all about – a spirit of discovery, a sense of adventure, and the opportunity to experience the world in unexpected ways,” stated Chris Prelog, president of Windstar Cruises.

According to recent reports, “There’s something special about stepping aboard without knowing exactly where the journey will take you and trusting that incredible experiences await. The enthusiasm we’ve seen for these sailings has been remarkable, and we’re excited to continue bringing this unique concept to new destinations around the world.”.

Throughout the voyage, guests had the opportunity to experience the destinations through shore excursions showcasing the region’s history, culture and gastronomy.

Experiences ranged from coastal hiking adventures and explorations of historic fortresses to visits to local wineries, villages and regional culinary experiences.

As previously reported by Cruise Industry News, two additional Mystery Cruises are planned for 2027: the Northern Europe Mystery Cruise aboard the Star Pride and the Japan Mystery Cruises aboard the Star Seeker.

Transcend Cruises has introduced its inaugural CEO-in-Residence Program, where its CEO Edie Rodriguez will spend a month sailing the Rhine onboard the Transcend Connect.

As a newly appointed CEO and board member, Rodriguez will run daily executive operations and leadership meetings from the ship between November 23 and December 22, 2026.

In what is mentioned to be the first time a cruise line CEO has spent an entire month onboard on either a river or cruise vessel, Rodriguez will meet with the onboard crew, charter clients and their guests and partners to help evolve Transcend’s brand strategy and product offering.

Corporate charters, MICE planners, travel advisors and affinity groups will also be able to connect and discuss customized itineraries and onboard experiences.

“Transcend Cruises was created to reimagine how groups come together on the rivers of Europe, turning every vessel into a customizable floating venue,” said Rodriguez.

“Setting up my office onboard for a month allows me stay close to our crew and operations and collaborate directly with clients and partners, and to experience the journeys just as they do and to better understand areas where we can improve as we continue to grow.”.

As the first charter-only river cruise firm with ships built exclusively for the group, Transcend welcomed its first ship, the Connect this summer, embarking on its first voyage on August 3, 2026.

Two additional ships are right now under construction, with intends for the fleet to reach four in 2028 and ultimately grow to 12 ships.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., remarked Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

“I know it’s going to be my main push,” he remarked. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

Sources indicate that democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

According to recent reports, “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators noted. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., stated earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

Sources indicate that while ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the upcoming Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how swiftly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, said that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

Sources indicate that democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

According to recent reports, "I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries mentioned.

It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro mentioned earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

Sources indicate that the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks noted. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

The Azamara Quest is right now wrapping up a drydock in Elefsis to become the first ship to undergo refurbishment as part of the Azamara Forward program.

After wrapping up its summer season in Piraeus, the vessel arrived at a Greek shipyard on October 31, 2026.

As part of the project, the 2000-built ship is getting a new deck with more staterooms, in addition to refreshed public rooms, as well as new venues, such as the Atlas Bar.

All staterooms are also being updated with upcoming finishes, improved lighting and design details aimed at enhancing comfort.

Sources indicate that the new Penthouse Deck adds 12 additional suites. The new premium staterooms will also introduce two new suite categories to the company’s fleet: Panorama and Grandview.

“We have designed these suites to have that calming, welcoming environment of a home away from home feeling for our guests,” said Martha Brabham, vice president of design and revitalization.

“So we would love our guests to enjoy the color scheme, the palette. We curated the elements in the room to really immerse you into that ocean experience.”.

Upon completion of the enhancements, the Azamara Quest is now scheduled to welcome guests back on November 26, 2026.

The ship is then set to offer itineraries in the Mediterranean, the Atlantic and the Caribbean before kicking off Azamara’s annual World Cruise in 2027.

“As the ship undergoes drydock, there’s a lot of work happening behind the scenes to bring Azamara Forward to life,” Azamara mentioned in a status patch.

“From refreshed spaces to thoughtful enhancements throughout the ship, every detail is coming together as the transformation takes shape,” the company added.

All ships in the company’s fleet are scheduled to undergo refurbishments as part of the Azamara Forward program.

The Azamara Onward will undergo the refit next, entering drydock in late 2027, followed by the Azamara Journey in late 2028.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steve Reynolds has spent his first few months as CEO of Variety Cruises building the systems he believes will carry the family-owned small-ship tech giant through its next stage of growth.
  • Reynolds was appointed in late October, with Filippos Venetopoulos, the third-generation head of the 77-year-old manufacturer, moving to executive chairman.
  • He said he found a brand with a strong product and a story not yet fully told.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steve Reynolds has spent his first few months as CEO of Variety Cruises building the systems he believes will carry the family-owned small-ship tech giant through its next stage of growth.

Reynolds was appointed in late October, with Filippos Venetopoulos, the third-generation head of the 77-year-old manufacturer, moving to executive chairman. Reynolds joined from Discover Qatar, the destination management company of Qatar Airways Group, where he was senior vice president.

He said he found a brand with a strong product and a story not yet fully told.

“The brand represents a style of travel, and as a style of travel it’s quite unique,” Reynolds told Cruise Industry News.

At its heart, he explained, Variety is an island-hopping product, and that kind of trip can be hard to manage alone.

It has been revealed that “It sounds all very romantic, island hopping, until you actually do it,” he remarked. “If you want to do it using ferries, transfers and hotels, it can be tiring and logistically tough.”.

He compared the model to river cruising, where guests unpack once and wake up somewhere new.

His test for a small ship is simple.

“If you can’t swim off the back, it’s not a small ship,” he noted.

Variety operates eight ships, with Greece as its core market. In 2027 the organization will add a Croatia product that also visits Montenegro. The Balearics, Corsica and the Italian islands are under consideration, depending on seasonal deployment and fleet logistics.

According to recent reports, north America is Variety’s lead source market, with solid contributions from the U.K., Europe, Australia and Newly introduced Zealand. Charters remain crucial, especially alumni and educational travel such as Road Scholar, and tour operators also sell the product under their own brands. Direct bookings are also growing.

The near-term goal, Reynolds mentioned, is to fill the existing fleet year-round before deciding whether to build, lease, buy or expand capacity.

Variety has started building a data warehouse to centralize customer and operational data, improve guest communication throughout the trip and use AI to automate processes and connect systems.

On his second day, Reynolds wrote about a dozen priority themes on his office whiteboard, including hyper-personalization, 2027 budgeting, reporting dashboards and guest quality metrics.

Much of how the business has always worked is good, he mentioned, but “if you can underpin that with strong principles around governance and using data to make and validate decisions, they tend to be much better decisions.”.

Reynolds mentioned southern hemisphere travelers who usually connect through Middle East hubs have become more cautious and are booking later. Europe is less affected, and North American demand for the Mediterranean, Seychelles and Tahiti remains steady.

He urged travelers to book while promotions last.

“My hope is in 12 months’ time we will have sold to an extent that there’ll be fewer of those deals available,” he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has declared a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

Sen. Chris Van Hollen revealed Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of Latest York, the current Democratic leader.

Recent findings suggest that van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has remarked since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

In a recent development, “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen remarked in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”.

Schumer has already stated he has the votes needed to continue serving as the leader.

Recent findings suggest that “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the key work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our latest Democratic majority and delivering for the American people,” Schumer mentioned in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that schumer's supporters were quick to highlight the success at the ballot box in 2026, with the Democratic caucus potentially growing to 56 seats if former Rep. Mary Peltola prevails in Alaska.

“Chuck has outlined an aggressive blueprint for the new Democratic majority which is directly responsive to the message we heard from the voters, and he has the experience and unique mastery of the Senate process to make it happen,” Sen. Angus King, a Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, said in a statement. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?”.

Industry observers note that in keeping with the World Series theme, Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., echoed King with her own statement of support for Schumer.

In a recent development, “The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time to change our management," Baldwin remarked. "The same is true in the Senate.”.

In an interview with MS NOW about his run, Van Hollen conceded that Schumer would be the favorite in the secret-ballot contest, which will take place in December.

“Am I the underdog? Yes,” Van Hollen stated. “You’re talking about an incumbent who uses the power of incumbency to, you know, provide deals to people.”.

Van Hollen outlined legislative priorities including restoring Medicaid funding that Republicans cut in last year's budget reconciliation law and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits. But he suggested Democrats need to go further.

"We need to extend tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but we can’t stop there, right? We have a completely broken health care system. It’s become profits, not people. And so my view is, we also need in the first 100 days to make health care more affordable for tens of millions of people," Van Hollen remarked. "We need to immediately make it clear that nobody’s going to pay one penny to subsidize data centers. ... We need to make sure that we have a livable minimum wage.".

He also mentioned he would not take sides in contested Democratic primaries, and he would make sure the DSCC did not take money from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC.

Van Hollen's early backers include progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who emerged from a hotly contested Democratic primary in Michigan while the Senate Democratic political apparatus was backing Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.

“In April, I was the first candidate in the country to call on Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, and I am proud to stand with him in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader,” El-Sayed said in a statement. “Michiganders demand money out of politics, money in pockets, and Medicare for All. Sen. Chris Van Hollen offers both the courage to go toe-to-toe with the Trump administration to deliver for working people and the experience to maneuver the Senate caucus. It’s why he has my full support to lead our caucus.”.

Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

On November 14 at the Plaque & Key Exchange, Broward County Vice-Mayor Michael Udine and Commissioner Steve Geller bestowed the Key to the County while Morris presented a commemorative plaque to Legend of the Seas’ Captain Sindre Borsheim.

All three captains also received the port’s Challenge Coins.

2026 was another record year for the Port, in which it welcomed 5.38 million guests.

In a recent development, this season, it will host 40 different cruise ships from nine lines. Apart from the three mentioned above, this includes Celebrity Cruises, Cunard Line, Disney Cruise Line, Holland America Line, Princess Cruises and Viking Ocean Cruises.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A recent short sailing onboard Royal Caribbean’s Oasis of the Seas became a cruise to nowhere due to adverse weather conditions.

Departing from Fort Lauderdale on November 16, 2026, the vessel was initially scheduled to operate a four-night cruise to the Bahamas.

The sailing’s original itinerary included visits to Nassau, as well as Royal Caribbean’s private island destination of Perfect Day CocoCay.

The ship initially cancelled its visit to Nassau before being forced to skip the call to the private destination as well.

“Adverse weather conditions producing high winds and ocean swells impacted our operations at Perfect Day CocoCay, preventing us from safely welcoming guests ashore,” Royal Caribbean mentioned in a statement shared with guests onboard.

“As a result, we won’t be able to visit the port and will instead enjoy a relaxing day at sea,” the organization continued.

Royal Caribbean added that any shore excursion booked through the tech giant for the destination would be automatically cancelled and refunded to their original form of payment.

According to recent reports, “We truly appreciate your understanding and flexibility regarding this unexpected change. To thank you for your continued loyalty and to help make up for the inconvenience we are pleased to offer a non-refundable onboard credit,” the firm continued.

Industry observers note that the credit was based on passengers’ cabin category and occupancy, with inside and outside cabins receiving $50, while balcony cabins received $75 and suites received $150. Cabins with third, fourth or more guests received a $25 extra credit per additional person.

“We’re sorry for this last-minute change caused by the weather – your safety is our top priority,” Royal Caribbean added.

Having repositioned from Latest Jersey earlier this month, the Oasis of the Seas is currently offering a series of short cruises to the Bahamas from Fort Lauderdale.

The three- and four-night itineraries will be offered through April 2027 and are highlighted by regular visits to Perfect Day CocoCay.

  • As part of the expanded season, the MSC Musica will mark the brand’s return to Paranaguá, a port on the Southern Brazilian coast after a two-year absence, offering weeklong cruises to Rio de Janeiro, Búzios, Ilhabela and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MSC Cruises recently kicked off its 2026-27 season in South America, which will see five ships sailing from eight homeports in Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina.

As part of the expanded season, the MSC Musica will mark the brand’s return to Paranaguá, a port on the Southern Brazilian coast after a two-year absence, offering weeklong cruises to Rio de Janeiro, Búzios, Ilhabela and more.

Other highlights of the deployment include the debut of the MSC Virtuosa, which will become the largest vessel to operate in South America, and the return to the MSC Seaview.

The MSC Divina and the MSC Splendida will also sail in the region, offering three- to nine-night itineraries from Santos, Rio de Janeiro, Itajaí, Balneário Camboriú, Buenos Aires, Salvador and Maceió.

Speaking during a ceremony onboard the MSC Divina, Adrian Ursilli, MSC’s country manager in Brazil, said that the firm’s expansion reflects a broader recognition of the industry’s economic impact and its overall importance, not only within the industry, but also various levels of government.

“Authorities increasingly view the activity as an crucial economic driver and job generator for the country, alongside its role in cultural exchange and well-being,” he added, noting that the addition of latest cruise terminals and destinations has also contributed to the development of the Brazilian market.

However, Ursilli stressed that port expansion must go hand in hand with structural reforms and objective solutions to keep South America attractive for global fleet deployment and solve other bottlenecks that still affect the industry, as well as other sectors of the economy.

Mentioning an upcoming tax reform, he stated that clarity and a path forward are needed to reduce the cost burden and make the country more competitive to attract further investment, since South America is competing for deployment with other markets, such as the Caribbean, Europe and Asia.

Industry observers note that “Right now, Brazil needs to be more competitive in terms of operational costs, port infrastructure, and legal certainty. These items make up our agenda of discussions with federal, state, and municipal governments so we can truly open the horizon for more sustainable future development.”.

The company confirmed further growth for South America in 2027-28, with the larger MSC Meraviglia replacing the MSC Seaview for itineraries to Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay.

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” said Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., seen above. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday did little to quell bipartisan demands from Congress for an accounting of potential national security fallout from his affair with an alleged Chinese spy and talk of adding tougher chip export controls to the annual defense authorization bill.

Industry observers note that huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, and reports say that it was with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean tech manufacturer and Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom the U.S. government believes spied for China, according to recent reports. The Latest York Times and Reuters reported he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees.

Sources indicate that senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told reporters Thursday that he supports the Senate investigating Huang’s potential influence on U.S. artificial intelligence and chip policy.

“I think that it would make sense because of the… nature of the association… and the governments and the national security interests we were talking about here,” Thune remarked, though he said he thought it would be “wrong” to make assumptions about how close Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump has been.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., echoed the need for lawmakers to delve into the scandal, saying in a post on X that “Congress must demand answers.”.

“The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?” Schumer wrote, referring to the president having invited Huang to accompany him to China in May.

It has been revealed that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said at a press conference that Reps. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and Jim Himes, D-Conn., the ranking members of the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, respectively, are leading Democrats’ efforts to “get to the bottom of what has happened.”.

“We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation,” Jeffries mentioned. “And to the extent that our national security has been compromised, the American people deserve answers, and we're going to work to make sure that happens.”.

The investigations look likely to begin before control of Congress changes hands in January.

It has been revealed that rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who chairs the House select China committee, told reporters that his panel, along with House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence, are in negotiations with Huang to find a date for his testimony before Congress.

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” Moolenaar mentioned. “What ways is Chinese intelligence influencing his perspective, his perspective influencing national security policy?”.

In a recent development, last week, the chairs of the three committees sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear at a joint closed-door briefing. Moolenaar mentioned that if Huang does not agree to a date, the committees will subpoena him.

Late Thursday, he joined with House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., and House Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, R-Ark., in sending a new letter to Huang seeking a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1. They also wrote to Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter seeking a similar interview on Dec. 2. Separately, Mast wrote to Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce Department undersecretary for industry and security, seeking his appearance at a committee hearing on Dec. 3.

Moolenaar also said that Congress needs to understand what privileged information Chinese intelligence may have gained access to through Huang and how they may have tried to influence U.S. policy.

According to recent reports, “We need to have strong safeguards when it comes to our technology and export controls,” Moolenaar stated. “And [Huang has] been one of the strongest proponents for not having export controls. This shines a whole newly introduced light on that discussion.”.

Sources indicate that also late Thursday, Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C.,  sent a letter to Huang calling on him to appear at a Dec. 3 committee hearing and another letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify at a Dec. 10 hearing "regarding recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns.".

Industry observers note that A proposed manager’s amendment to the Senate's fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill (S 4784) contains several possibilities for those safeguards, including requirements for chip security mechanisms that would allow for verification if semiconductors are diverted to countries of concern and a ban on exporting certain very powerful chips to those countries. The House NDAA does not contain similar language.

However, House Armed Services Chair Mike D. Rogers, D-Ala., is open to the restrictions. He told reporters Wednesday that he “would like to see” semiconductor export controls in the NDAA, but that the Huang scandal had not changed his position.

Democratic Caucus Vice Chair Ted Lieu, D-Calif., told reporters on Thursday that after reports that the federal government had been aware of Huang’s affair with the alleged spy, the administration should have shared the information with Congress.

“The administration needs to be investigated for hiding this information from Congress and the American people,” he noted.

Lieu also suggested that Nvidia’s reported donation to the White House ballroom project influenced the Trump administration’s decision to allow the export of some powerful Nvidia chips to China.

In a recent development, “There is no reason to do that. That hurts our national security, and we have an opportunity right now to fix that in the upcoming National Defense Authorization,” Lieu said.

Recent findings suggest that mast stated the Huang revelations could give new momentum to including chip export rules in the NDAA. He also said that his “directive” on the issue came “straight from the admin” and informed his objectives on the committee.

Sources indicate that “Don't let chips be smuggled to China. Make sure that American companies get to buy them first,” Mast noted. “Make sure that the machines that make them don't get sold to them, even though it's the Dutch that make the machines. Make sure that they can't access it remotely.”.

Mast’s committee has advanced many of those priorities, including some of the language included in the NDAA.

In March, the committee on a unanimous vote advanced legislation known as the Chip Security Act, which would require chip security mechanisms to verify that certain semiconductors subject to export controls aren’t diverted to countries of concern, including China and Iran.

The committee also advanced bills to require the Bureau of Industry and Security and the State Department to work with allied suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to implement export controls to prevent the equipment from going to countries of concern, and to require licenses for the export of certain powerful chips, including banning exporting certain chips to countries of concern.

Versions of all three bills are included in the Senate manager’s amendment to the NDAA.

The scandal has also led to calls for oversight of the Commerce Department, including Secretary Howard Lutnick, for its handling of export policy and actions around Huang.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters Thursday that Lutnick and Nvidia should testify “before Democrats can set the narrative.”.

“If there is some reasonable basis or some way to discount some of the reporting, the best way to do it is request a meeting with us and give us a briefing,” Tillis remarked. “Because otherwise, you're going to get what you get in an oversight hearing in about six weeks.”.

Industry observers note that asked about oversight of the Commerce Department’s role in the Huang scandal, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who chairs the Commerce Committee, said his panel “has engaged in vigorous oversight under Republican presidents and Democrat presidents and will continue to be [engaged in it].”.

On Wednesday, prior to Huang’s resignation, Senate Banking ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller requesting that they “preserve all documents, communications, records, and other materials regarding the export of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China.”.

“This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” the senators wrote.

In a recent development, in a statement Thursday, Warren mentioned that Huang’s resignation did not “absolve” him of the need to answer questions. She also called for the passage of stricter export controls, including the bill to ban the export of certain chips to China.

Sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., sent his own letter on Wednesday to Lutnick, Rubio, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, requesting an patch on the Justice Department’s investigation into Megaspeed for possibly diverting U.S. chips to China.

Sources indicate that savannah Behrmann, John M. Donnelly, Jacob Fulton and David Jordan contributed to this report.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Avora Lumina LLC, the tech giant set to convert the Seven Seas Navigator from Regent Seven Seas Cruises into a residential cruise ship, filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition in the U.S.
  • The manufacturer stated it its filing that noncontingent liquidated debts are below the $3,424,000 threshold.
  • In the petition, Avora Lumina estimated its assets at $10 million to $50 million and its liabilities at $1 million to $10 million, with between one and 49 creditors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Avora Lumina LLC, the tech giant set to convert the Seven Seas Navigator from Regent Seven Seas Cruises into a residential cruise ship, filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Florida on Nov. 23, 2026.

The manufacturer stated it its filing that noncontingent liquidated debts are below the $3,424,000 threshold.

In the petition, Avora Lumina estimated its assets at $10 million to $50 million and its liabilities at $1 million to $10 million, with between one and 49 creditors.

The tech giant also remarked that funds will be available for distribution to unsecured creditors.

The petition was signed by Mikael Petterson, listed as founder and chairman. The organization is represented by Bradley S. Shraiberg of Shraiberg Page PA in Boca Raton, Florida.

Navigator Vessel Company LLC, based in Hamilton, Bermuda, was the only creditor listed with a specific claim amount, at $2.5 million.

The remaining entries on the list of the 20 largest unsecured creditors, including the Internal Revenue Service, the Florida Department of Revenue, the Broward County Tax Collector, the Securities and Exchange Commission and federal and state attorneys general offices, were listed “for information purposes” with amounts marked as unknown.

The petition indicated no bankruptcy filings by the manufacturer in the past eight years and no pending cases involving affiliates.

Avora Residences announced in March 2026 that it had acquired the Seven Seas Navigator from Regent Seven Seas Cruises through a nine-year charter with a nominal purchase option from Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings.

The 496-guest ship was set to debut in January 2028 as the Avora Lumina following a full luxury residential conversion, launching from Lisbon on a three-year global circumnavigation.

Plans called for 242 residences, with life-of-ship ownership priced from about $545,000 to $4.2 million and a five-year program starting at around $219,600.

Avora was founded by Petterson and Kathy Villalba, who also founded Villa Vie Residences.

Villa Vie suspended operations of the Villa Vie Odyssey in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, on Oct. 27, 2026, citing sharp increases in fuel costs, and said it was evaluating restructuring and recapitalization alternatives. The Villa Vie Odyssey left Cambodia without residents in early November.

How I Got My Visa to France

📅 16 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010.
  • But that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées.
  • Since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010. Friends I had met back in Thailand highlighted me around the area and introduced me to French culture. It was my first time in France and I loved the food, the wine, and the people.

But that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées. The lights, the energy, the mystique! There was magic in the air. I felt like I had known the city my entire life and I was simply returning home.

Since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart. Over the years, I spent countless visits exploring France and Paris in particular. I’ve run tours in the city and I spent a few months living there in 2019.

Last August, after yet another sojourn, I thought to myself, “What if I moved back?”.

Sources indicate that I was growing a bit tired of the NYC dating scene, the rising cost of living, and felt like, creatively, I was in a rut. With AI coming for creators like me and the industry changing, I was a little lost on what, career-wise, would come next.

And Paris seemed like the best place to go.

In a recent development, it’s cheaper than NYC, I had friends there already, I’ve always wanted to learn French, it would make a great base for exploring Europe, and I could start writing my next book there. There’s nothing like a change in scenery to get the creativity flowing!

But the question remained: how do you move to France?

After all, they don’t have a digital nomad visa, and you’re limited to three months if you visit on your regular Schengen tourist visa.

It has been revealed that well, it turns out that it’s not actually that hard. (And while I can only speak for Americans, I suspect the criteria are similar for Canadians, Aussies, Kiwis, and other “developed” nations.).

If you want to move to France, you have four main options:.

Sources indicate that the student visa is pretty straightforward. You need to enroll in a full-time university program and show you have enough funds to support yourself (around 600 Euros per month). A friend is at the moment there on this visa, as she is doing a nine-month intensive French program to become fluent. You still have to apply for the visa, but if you’re enrolled in an accredited school, you’ll likely get approved. Another benefit to this visa is that you can work part-time on it!

But this visa is contingent on being in school, so if you leave or quit, it’s voided. However, when you are done, you can change this to a “job seeker” visa, which can give you up to another six months in France (or more depending on how long your program was).

Sources indicate that I thought about applying for the entrepreneur visa, but the application process is pretty complex and can take months to be approved. You have to set up your business in France — and that is a lot of paperwork. You have to show that your business makes money, has clients (at least one of them being French), and can support you full-time (you have to make at least the French minimum wage). They will scrutinize your assets and financials a lot and you’ll need to register your business in France and pay French taxes.

Sources indicate that additionally, France offers a talent visa. If you’re an expert in your field (with verifiable accreditations and accolades), this could be a good visa to apply for, especially if you proposal to stay in France for a long time and want to physically work there. But, again, you’ll need to have some source of income and plan to do physical business in France. If you’re not an academic but someone in the arts, you have to show how you are going to add to the “culture of France” in some way.

While I would meet the requirements for both those visas, the process for either would have been time-consuming, and, since I’m not sure France is going to be my forever home, I decided not to go through that process.

So I went with the long-term visitor visa, officially called VLS-TS visiteur. This allows me to stay up to 12 months in France and is renewable in the country. It does come with a lot of restrictions, however: I can’t physically work here and I am not allowed into the French social welfare system.

Industry observers note that it’s also the visa a lot of Americans (and most retirees) are coming in on. If you have passive income or retirement savings and just want to live in France, this is a good option for you. It allows you to set up a bank account and it can be renewed pretty much indefinitely.

The paperwork for this visa (which I’ll get into in a bit) essentially comes down to whether or not you can support yourself. French authorities want to make sure you won’t be a burden on the system.

It has been revealed that my biggest question centered around whether or not I could “work” on this visa. A lot of creators and digital nomads are applying for — and getting — this visa.

But remember: you aren’t allowed to work on this visa so how are you going to work if you can’t work?

So let me take a moment to talk about “work” from a legal standpoint.

It has been revealed that as I mentioned, there’s no digital nomad visa that allows you to work in France. And the French tax office said last July that remote work is considered taxable — but there are no official laws that say so. That’s just their opinion and there’s been no progress in codifying that opinion. In fact, my visa doesn’t even come with a tax number, so I can’t be taxed. I couldn’t pay taxes even if I wanted to.

The visa office asks how you’ll support yourself when you are in France and one of the sources of income they accept is “income from work.” I was very open that my means of support would be the income from this blog and my books.

The system there really hasn’t caught up to remote work. It still defines “work” as something you do physically that could take away a job from a French person.

So could I run walking tours in Paris? Nope. Could you work at a café? Nope.

But does writing this blog post count as work? After all, no one is paying for it. It’s a free resource. Does going to a café to work on the next great American novel count? What about my weekly newsletter that has affiliate links (that generate income) in it? Is writing that considered work?

Sources indicate that the gray area is considerable, so the best thing to do is to talk to a lawyer. I recommend Daniel Tostado (yes, that’s his real name), one of the biggest American-French immigration lawyers in Paris. He has a huge law firm and regularly meets with government officials to clarify the rules on this. He gave me some solid advice.

For this long-term visitor visa, the application process is pretty easy. You go to the French government website, fill out your application, take the application number to the TLScontact website, and make an appointment. (France outsources the appointment process to this company, which then sends everything to the French consulate for approval.).

The main things you’ll want to demonstrate are that you have accommodation for 90 days on your application and enough income to support yourself. They just want to make sure you aren’t going to be a burden on the system. I went overboard. Here’s what I brought to my appointment:.

I didn’t need the second bank account, tax returns, or W-2 (they weren’t required) but the woman at the appointment stated the more proof you had the better and it wouldn’t hurt. And another friend who got this visa didn’t bring anything beyond what was asked in the application form. But I wanted to take no chances!

At the appointment, the staff double-checks your paperwork, takes your biometric data, collects the fees, and then sends your passport to the embassy for processing. Officially, it takes up to 15 days to process your visa, but everyone I know seems to get it back within a week.

In a recent development, the worst part was not knowing if you are approved until your passport is returned. While you can track the progress of your application, you don’t know the verdict until your passport is back in your hands. While I was waiting (and anxiously spiraling), I looked on Reddit and found that most denials were for lack of income or concerns with their accommodation, which seem to be the two most notable things to have perfect on your application.

Once you get your visa back, you can enter France any time after the start date. After you enter, you have 90 days to register your visa with the state (they give you a little QR code with instructions). This allows you to “officially” be on this long-term visa. (It’s a more paperwork kind of thing.).

Once that is done, there’s nothing else to do and you can stay in France (and Europe) until your visa expires!

So, if you’re considering moving to France, these are your options. But, as always, I’m not a lawyer and this is not legal advice. In regard to work and other problems or questions, it’s important that you seek legal counsel and get their expert opinion!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Costa Diadema opened the 2026-27 cruise season in Maceió, Brazil, which is set to feature over 25 calls and bring approximately 150,000 tourists to the area.

The Costa Cruises vessel docked at the Brazilian port on November 19, 2026, completing its trans-Atlantic crossing that started in Italy.

Continuing its trans-Atlantic crossing, the ship is scheduled to visit other destinations in Brazil before kicking off the firm’s 2026-27 season in South America later this month.

The lineup in Maceió is highlighted by the 4,888-passenger MSC Virtuosa, which will be the largest ship sailing in South America this season.

The ship is scheduled to make weekly calls at the port in Alagoas state during its seven-night cruises from Santos, with guests also being able to board the ship on select dates.

Maceió will also welcome other ships from MSC Cruises, in addition to vessels from Phoenix Reisen, Costa Cruises and Corazul Cruceros.

Another highlight of the 2026-27 season is an inaugural visit by Carnival Cruise Line’s Firenze, scheduled to arrive in Maceió for a transit call in February while repositioning from the West Coast to the Caribbean.

“Every ship that arrives in Maceió means increased business for restaurants, retail, and sightseeing tours, as well as more opportunities for those who live here,” mentioned Maceió’s Mayor Rodrigo Cunha.

In a recent development, “That is why we invest in tourism, in enhancing our public spaces, and in preparing the city to better welcome visitors. We want this growth to translate into jobs, income, and opportunities for the people of Maceió.”.

According to the Maceió Port Authority, a special reception operation will be in place to welcome cruise passengers arriving through the end of the season in April.

  • The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept. 22. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.

The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.

And it would bump funding for the Government Accountability Office up to $860 million, an increase of nearly 6 percent from fiscal 2026. That stands in contrast to the version of the bill advanced by the House Appropriations Committee in May, which floated slashing the GAO by 25 percent.

It joins several other draft spending bills released this week by Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, who is trying to kickstart bicameral negotiations as lawmakers stare down a Dec. 11 deadline to fund the government.

Her committee ran into a stalemate on topline numbers earlier this year that stopped it from marking up any of the 12 annual bills, but lawmakers nipped the threat of a government shutdown in the bud ahead of the midterm elections by pushing through a continuing resolution. With that funding now set to expire next month, appropriators are hoping they can wrap up at least some of the bills while punting the rest into the next Congress with another stopgap.

In a recent development, the Legislative Branch bill is the smallest of the 12 appropriations bills and typically among the least controversial. But debates over the GAO have become a sticking point during the Trump administration as the agency accuses the White House of violating budget laws — a move the Office of Management and Budget has pushed back on, arguing the GAO has no authority over the administration since it is part of the legislative branch.

Industry observers note that the GAO has been without a permanent head after its longtime leader Gene L. Dodaro retired last year, although Republicans are now making a last-ditch effort to get one confirmed during the lame-duck session before Democrats take power.

Industry observers note that the House version of the spending bill sought to bar the comptroller general from suing under the 1974 budget law restricting presidential impoundments, unless specifically authorized by Congress. But the Senate proposal includes no such language, and overall, it appears designed to avoid drastic or contentious moves.

It would also leave in place a provision that would block cost-of-living adjustments for members of Congress, whose pay has been frozen since 2009.

Senate Democrats, however, criticized the bill text after its release, saying it wouldn’t invest enough in the legislative branch.

“The Legislative Branch bill underfunds key work to support oversight of the Executive Branch, and it underfunds important efforts to keep the Capitol complex safe,” Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., mentioned in a statement.

Sources indicate that the Architect of the Capitol would get $762.5 million, though funding for House office buildings is not included in that total. The agency is requesting $1.6 billion as it seeks to begin large-scale renovations of the Rayburn House Office Building. The architect has repeatedly warned lawmakers that parts of the Capitol complex are in need of critical infrastructure upgrades, arguing that delaying renovations will only make them more expensive as things continue to deteriorate.

The bill’s $5.3 billion proposal represents funding for the Senate and legislative branch agencies, while excluding House-only funds, which are typically added later.

Mein Schiff 3 will set sail on its first cruise following its collision in Bremerhaven with a temporary lifeboat solution, while three upcoming lifeboats will be delivered at a later date.

As reported by Schiffe und Kreuzfahrten, the lifeboats need to be manufactured anew after they were destroyed in a collision with a container ship at the end of October while the ship was leaving Bremerhaven in stormy conditions on its way to Spain.

Since the forward lifeboats on the starboard side, including their superstructures, have not yet been repaired, the ship will likely receive additional life rafts to ensure that there are sufficient spaces available for the unlikely event of an evacuation.

New lifeboats, which are expected to be produced over the next few months, can then be taken onboard when the ship calls at port.

At the time of the collision, the port authority stated that lifeboats, their associated cranes and the outer hull were damaged on the cruise ship during the incident.

TUI confirmed last week that the next scheduled cruise following repairs at Lloyd Wrft Bremerhaven will go ahead as planned, departing on Saturday, November 28, 2026.

Captain Günter Batzner is set to command the bridge during this first cruise to Kiel, where he will be replaced by Captain Alexander Orendt, the ship’s regular captain who is set to return following vacation.

According to recent reports, they will replace Captain Jan F. Schubert, who commanded the ship when the collision happened, as he is under investigation by the Bremen maritime police to determine whether he breached his duty of care by departing in adverse weather conditions.

The Galveston Wharves has announced the appointment of Kathy Thomas as its director of communications, formalizing a leadership role she has supported as a consultant to the port for the past seven years.

“Over the past seven years, Thomas has become an integral part of our team and has developed a deep understanding of our operations, our priorities and the important role the port plays in Galveston and the Texas economies,” said Rodger Rees, Galveston Wharves’ port director and CEO.

“As our port continues to grow and diversify, effective communications are more crucial than ever. Bringing Thomas onto our leadership team is a natural next step and will strengthen our ability to tell the port’s story, build relationships and keep our community and stakeholders informed.”.

Thomas leads the port’s communications and public relations efforts, overseeing strategic communications, media relations, crisis communications, community outreach, special events and digital content.

In a press release, the port mentioned that she plays a key role in communicating the port’s growing cruise, cargo and commercial operations; major capital development projects; and economic contributions to the region.

During her years as a consultant, Thomas crafted the port’s business-based strategic communications structure, directed the port’s 200th anniversary, released the port’s new website and organized several cruise, cargo and public engagement events.

It has been revealed that thomas brings communications experience to her role. As owner of Community Strategies, LLC, she provided a range of services to major energy, petrochemical and health care organizations.

It has been revealed that she began her career in journalism at the Galveston County Daily News, where she was managing editor. She holds a Bachelor of Journalism degree from The University of Texas at Austin.
